stories.head: OpenAI projects $100B in ad revenue by 2030 as it makes ChatGPT ads easier to buy
stories.plain: OpenAI is opening ChatGPT to paid advertising and claiming it will generate $100 billion in ad revenue by 2030. That would rival Google's current ad business. The piece questions whether advertisers will actually follow. For marketers, this signals a serious new channel — and a potential shift in where budgets flow away from traditional search.

stories.head: SEOPulse launches enterprise platform to track brand visibility inside AI answer engines
stories.plain: A new benchmark study finds traditional search has lost roughly half its traffic to AI answer engines, and AI models agree on top brands in fewer than 1.5% of queries. SEOPulse now offers real-user session tracking across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini. This is a concrete product built around GEO — exactly the measurement gap marketers need to close.

stories.head: Qlik brings governed analytics context to AI agents via AWS and Databricks Marketplace
stories.plain: Qlik's MCP server — which feeds governed, transformation-ready data into AI agents — is now available directly in AWS and Databricks marketplaces. This lowers the barrier for enterprise teams to wire trusted business context into agentic workflows without bespoke integration work, making reliable data-driven AI decisions easier to deploy at scale.

stories.head: Alchemer Iris launches as AI-native platform that turns customer feedback into automated action
stories.plain: Alchemer Iris unifies surveys, reviews, and reputation signals into one AI layer that guides next actions and routes work between systems automatically. Rather than just surfacing insights, it closes the loop by pushing tasks to the right teams. This shifts feedback tools from reporting to agentic decisioning, which matters for how CX budgets get justified.

stories.head: Adobe integrates 70+ creative tools into Slack via MCP, enabling in-channel content generation
stories.plain: Adobe's new Slack MCP app lets marketing teams generate and edit content without leaving their collaboration workspace, using campaign context already present in Slack threads. This is a concrete example of the Model Context Protocol moving from developer experiment to everyday creative workflow, with implications for how martech stacks get assembled going forward.

stories.head: OpenAI's $100 Billion Ad Revenue Projection for ChatGPT by 2030
stories.plain: OpenAI is building out a ChatGPT ad business and projecting $100 billion in ad revenue by 2030. This matters because AI answer engines replacing search would fundamentally shift where marketing budgets go — and whether brands can even buy visibility inside AI-generated answers. The gap between the claim and current evidence is enormous.

stories.head: AI Agents in Your Tech Stack Are Leaking Proprietary and Customer Data
stories.plain: When AI agents pass data between systems to run campaigns autonomously, each handoff is a potential leak of proprietary strategy or customer PII. This piece explains the specific vulnerabilities and what governance controls are missing in most autonomous marketing stacks — critical reading for anyone building or buying agentic tools.

stories.head: Marketers Are Giving AI More Authority While Knowing the Underlying Data Is Bad
stories.plain: A study finds marketers are expanding AI decision-making power even while acknowledging their CRM data is unreliable. Bad input data means AI decisions and revenue attribution are systematically wrong — yet the automation keeps spreading. This is a governance and CDP quality problem that affects every downstream AI use case.

stories.head: SEOPulse Launches Enterprise Platform to Track Brand Visibility Inside AI Answer Engines
stories.plain: A new benchmark study reports traditional search has lost 50% of traffic to AI answer engines like ChatGPT and Perplexity, and AI models agree on top brands in fewer than 1.5% of queries. SEOPulse launches real-user session tracking across these engines. GEO is becoming a measurable, manageable discipline — not just a theory.

stories.head: Optimizely Releases Purpose-Built Marketing AI Models at a Fraction of Generic LLM Cost
stories.plain: Optimizely claims its new family of post-trained, task-specific AI models matches frontier-LLM quality for marketing tasks at roughly one-tenth the cost. This shifts the build-vs-buy calculus for marketing AI — purpose-built small models may outperform and underprice general-purpose giants for specific content and decisioning jobs.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: Search Is Dying; Answer Engines Rule Now
body: Traditional search rankings have lost roughly 50% of their traffic to AI answer engines in the past year, forcing an entirely new discipline — AI visibility optimization — to emerge almost overnight. Brands that relied on blue-link SEO now find their content bypassed entirely unless AI systems can find, trust, and cite them.

The decision that changes is where you invest content & measurement effort. Optimizing for click-through rates is secondary to being the source an LLM quotes. Platforms like SEOPulse and guidance on what it takes for AI to act on your brand signal that AIO (AI Optimization) is becoming a mandatory budget line.
ev: MarTech · AI find & trust your brand

themes.head: Agentic AI Moves Into Production Workflows
body: The month's product launches — Celigo Ora, Omilia's self-learning agentic CX, Alchemer Iris, and Qlik's MCP expansion — share a single pattern: AI is no longer advising humans, it is completing tasks end-to-end. These agents pull live business context, decide on actions, and execute across systems without a human in the loop for each step.

This shifts the governance question from 'what does the AI recommend?' to 'what is the AI allowed to do?' The MarTech piece on the terrifying loophole in autonomous stacks underlines that most organizations have not yet answered that question before deployment, creating real operational and legal exposure.

themes.head: The Real Cost of AI Is Data, Not Compute
body: Multiple pieces this month converge on an uncomfortable truth: AI ROI calculations are badly distorted because teams are not counting data preparation, token-level data taxes, and the ongoing cost of feeding clean context to models. Domo's Ben Schein frames it as a 'data tax per token' — every prompt costs something, and most budgets ignore it.

Compounding this, a MarTech survey found that marketers already know their AI is running on bad data yet are proceeding anyway. The decision that changes here is the sequencing: data quality & governance investment must come before — not after — AI deployment, or every ROI projection is fiction.
ev: Agile Brand · data tax per token

themes.head: MCP Becomes the Connective Tissue of the Stack
body: The Model Context Protocol is fast becoming the default plumbing layer between AI agents and enterprise tools. Adobe plugged 70+ Creative & Document tools into Slack via MCP; Qlik extended MCP across AWS & Databricks so agents can pull trusted business context on demand. MCP is being treated as infrastructure, not a feature.

For MarTech buyers this means vendor evaluation now includes an 'MCP-ready?' checkbox alongside API availability. Teams that standardize on MCP-compatible tools early will be able to swap or stack AI agents without re-integration work — a meaningful long-term cost and agility advantage.
ev: Adobe · 70+ tools into Slack via MCP

themes.head: Measurement Is Broken and Marketers Are the Problem
body: Two sharp MarTech pieces this month make the case that measurement failure is a behavior problem, not a tool problem. Marketers choose metrics that validate spend rather than ones that reveal truth, and the proliferation of AI-generated signals has made it easier than ever to cherry-pick a favorable number. The only reliable signal left, per one piece, is what ads actually caused — incremental lift measured through controlled experiments.

This matters because every AI optimization loop — bidding, personalization, content — is only as good as the feedback signal it trains on. If measurement is corrupted by confirmation bias & vanity metrics, AI amplifies those errors at scale rather than correcting them. Fixing governance around measurement is therefore a prerequisite for trustworthy AI marketing.

month.takeaway: Every major move this month — agentic automation, MCP plumbing, AI answer engines, token-cost accounting — ultimately stalls unless marketers first fix the unglamorous foundation: clean data, honest measurement, and governance that precedes deployment rather than chasing it.
